stories.headline: Opposition parties accuse Majhi government of mishandling flood situation in Odisha
stories.title: Opposition parties accuse Majhi government of mishandling flood situation in Odisha
stories.summary: ‘It is deeply unfortunate that Ganjam has been set back by several years due to negligence by the State government,’ says BJD supremo Naveen Patnaik
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Biju Janata Dal and the Congress on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) accused the Mohan Charan Majhi-led BJP government in Odisha of mishandling disasters, particularly the floods in Ganjam district, alleging that its failure to manage the situation had compounded people’s suffering.

In a letter addressed to the Chief Minister, BJD supremo and Leader of the Opposition Naveen Patnaik said, “The floods have caused massive damage to infrastructure, extensive crop losses, loss of lives and destruction of livelihoods.
It is deeply unfortunate that Ganjam has been set back by several years due to negligence by the State government.”
“A Standard Operating Procedure in cyclone and flood management is to release adequate water from dams prior to rains.
However, in the case of Ganjam, water from the dams was released by the Water Resources Department after the onset of heavy cyclonic rains.
This compounded the floods and caused huge loss to life and property,” Mr. Patnaik pointed out.
“People have complained that adequate warning was not given to them before the gates were opened.
This gross negligence and manmade crisis raise serious issues of accountability.
People are demanding strict action against those responsible for such a serious lapses,” he said.
Alleging delay in providing relief to flood-hit people, the former Chief Minister said, “just paying lip service will not work.

A focused whole of government approach should be undertaken to provide timely compensation and to boost the confidence of farmers, women, youth, small traders and the common people of Ganjam district.”

“Being a coastal State, Odisha will always remain vulnerable to natural disasters and hence with sustained effort and foresight, the BJD government had built a community based, resilient, disaster management system that is globally acclaimed.

stories.headline: Election Commission enforces strict political neutrality for re-employed officials in poll-bound States
stories.title: Election Commission enforces strict political neutrality for re-employed officials in poll-bound States
stories.summary: The Commission reiterated that contractual or re-employed status does not exempt personnel from strict compliance with the MCC code
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Election Commission of India (ECI) Tuesday issued an official directive enforcing political neutrality during the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) period in five-poll bound States of UP, Goa, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Manipur.
The order in particular puts under glare retired government officials who are re-engaged, contractually employed, or re-employed by State administrations.
The Chief Secretaries and Chief Electoral.
Officers of Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, and Uttarakhand, which will face assembly polls early next year to strictly enforce the directive by immediately sensitise all departments.
The said individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns or canvassing.

By invoking its foundational rulings—specifically referencing its historical directives No. 62/84 (dated November 6, 1984) and No. 62/91 (dated April 6, 1991)—the Commission reiterated that contractual or re-employed status does not exempt personnel from strict compliance with the MCC code.

Sources said, the ECI aims to eliminate any potential systemic bias where re-engaged veteran officials might use their administrative proximity to influence the electoral atmosphere or favour the ruling dispensations.
Any violation of political neutrality by these officials during the MCC period will invite swift and severe disciplinary action from the apex election body.

stories.headline: Kargil shuts down against winter polls as SEC announces December 4 election date
stories.title: Kargil shuts down against winter polls as SEC announces December 4 election date
stories.summary: Meanwhile, according to the schedule announced by the State Election Commission, November 17 is the last date for filing nomination papers
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Kargil district observed a complete shutdown on Tuesday against the holding of elections during the harsh winter months, even as the State Election Commission (SEC) announced December 4 as the polling date for all Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils.
The Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), an umbrella body of political, religious and civil society organisations, had called for the shutdown to protest the decision to hold elections during winter.
Shops and business establishments across the district remained closed in response to the call.
The alliance also organised a candlelight march in the evening under the banner of “Save Democracy”.
The KDA has opposed holding elections during the winter, when Ladakh experiences severe cold, with minimum temperatures often dropping to between minus 10 and minus 15 degrees Celsius.
The harsh conditions make travel and outdoor activities difficult, raising concerns over the participation of voters and candidates in the electoral process.
Meanwhile, according to the schedule announced by the State Election Commission, November 17 is the last date for filing nomination papers.
The scrutiny of nominations will take place on November 18, while candidates can withdraw their papers until November 20.
Polling for the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils will begin on December 4, with the entire election process scheduled to conclude by December 8.
The shutdown in Kargil came amid opposition from the KDA to the winter election schedule, even as the poll process moved forward with the announcement of dates.

stories.headline: FMCG companies see demand revival; weak monsoon, rising costs cloud outlook
stories.title: FMCG companies see demand revival; weak monsoon, rising costs cloud outlook
stories.summary: India's leading consumer goods companies appear to be entering a more encouraging phase of demand recovery, with the September quarter results of Hindustan Unilever, Dabur, Marico, Nestlé India, Britannia and Godrej Consumer Products pointing to improving volumes across several categories. But beneath the headline growth numbers, there are reasons for caution: An uneven monsoon, rising commodity costs and the possibility that rural consumption could lose momentum in the coming quarters.The September quarter was particularly strong for packaged foods and companies with a diversified product portfolio. Nestlé India reported a 20.5 percent increase in revenue from operations to Rs6,782 crore, while Britannia's product sales rose 16.6 percent to Rs5,542 crore. Both companies reported robust volume growth, suggesting that the improvement was not merely the result of price increases.Nestlé's consolidated net profit rose 36.3 percent to Rs1,027 crore, while Britannia reported a 10.8 percent increase to Rs726 crore. Nestlé's volume growth was in double digits, while Britannia reported volume growth of 13 percent."The quarter saw a continuation of strong and broad-based growth across all product groups," said Manish Tiwary, chairman and managing director of Nestlé India. The company also increased advertising and marketing expenditure by 46 percent, indicating that it is willing to invest in brands even as input costs remain a concern.Hindustan Unilever (HUL), India's largest consumer goods company, reported underlying sales growth of 15 percent, its highest in 14 quarters. Underlying volume growth was 7 percent, while net sales increased 14.5 percent to Rs18,226 crore. Its consolidated net profit, however, rose a more modest 4 percent to Rs2,790 crore, partly reflecting the comparison with the previous year and the impact of a Rs273 crore tax-related gain.HUL's home care business grew 22 percent, while its beauty and personal care portfolio continued to see improving momentum. CEO Priya Nair said the company had delivered strong volume growth, supported by its focus on brands and distribution. "The Indian economy remains resilient, with healthy macro indicators supporting a positive consumption environment," she said.The improvement was also visible at Marico, which reported 10 percent underlying volume growth in its India business. Consolidated revenue increased 12 percent to Rs3,897 crore, while net profit rose 31 percent to Rs550 crore. Its Ebitda margin expanded by 200 basis points to 18.2 percent, helped by a substantial moderation in copra prices.Marico's Parachute franchise recorded 13 percent volume growth, while its foods portfolio grew 45 percent. The performance suggests that the company is benefiting from both a recovery in its core business and the expansion of newer categories. Managing Director and CEO Saugata Gupta, however, said the company was watching the impact of deficient rainfall and inflation on rural consumption. He told Moneycontrol that it was particularly watchful of demand patterns in regions affected by poor rainfall.Dabur and Godrej Consumer Products also reported double-digit revenue growth. Dabur's consolidated revenue rose 11.6 percent to Rs3,563 crore, with India FMCG business growth of 10.7 percent. Underlying volume growth in the domestic business was 5.5 percent. Its international business grew 20 percent in rupee terms, providing an additional source of momentum. Net profit increased 11.7 percent to Rs505 crore.Godrej Consumer Products reported 19 percent revenue growth to Rs4,413 crore, with underlying volume growth of 8 percent. Net profit increased nearly 14 percent to Rs523 crore. Its India business recorded 7 percent underlying volume growth, while Indonesia and Africa also contributed to the consolidated performance."We delivered strong broad-based underlying volume growth across India, Indonesia and Africa, despite subdued monsoon conditions in India," said Aasif Malbari, managing director and CEO of Godrej Consumer Products.Also Read: How No-Cost-EMIs have changed the way Indians shopThe rural demand questionThe results are encouraging, but the monsoon presents a potential complication. India's Southwest monsoon ended with rainfall around 12.5 percent below normal, worse than the India Meteorological Department's forecast. The shortfall was particularly pronounced in parts of southern and eastern India, raising concerns about agricultural output, farm incomes and the next cropping season.Rural consumption has been relatively resilient over the past few quarters, and companies have continued to report healthy demand in smaller towns and villages. Data from retail intelligence platform Bizom indicated that rural markets continued to outperform urban markets in Q2FY27. However, the gap narrowed considerably, with rural growth no longer running at the four-to-five times multiple seen in previous quarters.The concern is that the impact of deficient rainfall may not be immediately visible in consumer spending. A weaker harvest, lower farm incomes and higher food inflation could gradually affect purchasing power, particularly among lower-income households. The impact is also likely to be more pronounced in discretionary categories than in everyday essentials.HUL's Nair has argued that higher minimum support prices and increased government spending on rural employment should provide some support to rural incomes. But brokerages remain watchful. Nomura has cautioned that the below-normal monsoon and the possibility of weaker agricultural output could put rural demand under pressure in the coming quarters.Also Read: Car sales fall 14 percent in October as buyers defer purchases to NovemberMargins are the next challengeFor consumer companies, the other concern is the rising cost of inputs. Crude-linked derivatives, palm oil and other vegetable oils have seen inflationary pressures, while geopolitical developments and currency movements have added uncertainty. Companies have so far attempted to balance selective price increases with cost-saving measures, mindful that aggressive pricing could derail the volume recovery.HUL's Ebitda margin declined year-on-year to around 22.6 percent, while Godrej Consumer Products' Ebitda growth of 12 percent trailed its 19 percent revenue growth. Dabur's operating margin also remained under pressure. In contrast, Marico benefited from lower copra prices, demonstrating how different commodity exposures can produce divergent margin outcomes across the sector.Nomura analyst Mihir Shah has also cautioned that the sharp pricing actions at HUL, combined with a weak monsoon and drought conditions in several states, could affect rural demand and volume growth in the coming quarters.The December quarter will therefore be an important test. Festive demand and the timing of Diwali purchases could support near-term sales, but the more important question is whether volume growth can hold up once the seasonal boost fades. For now, the results suggest that the consumer recovery is real. Whether it is durable will depend on the health of rural incomes, the trajectory of commodity prices and the ability of companies to grow volumes without compromising margins.

Dabur's operating margin also remained under pressure.
In contrast, Marico benefited from lower copra prices, demonstrating how different commodity exposures can produce divergent margin outcomes across the sector.

Nomura analyst Mihir Shah has also cautioned that the sharp pricing actions at HUL, combined with a weak monsoon and drought conditions in several states, could affect rural demand and volume growth in the coming quarters.
The December quarter will therefore be an important test.
Festive demand and the timing of Diwali purchases could support near-term sales, but the more important question is whether volume growth can hold up once the seasonal boost fades.
For now, the results suggest that the consumer recovery is real.

stories.headline: India remains key drug supplier to US amid push for self-reliance
stories.title: India remains key drug supplier to US amid push for self-reliance
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 10 : India's vast pharmaceutical manufacturing network has emerged as a critical pillar of the US healthcare system, highlighting the challenges facing American President Donald Trump's efforts to bring generic drug production back to the United States, according to a report. A report by The Star highlighted a manufacturing facility operated by a leading pharmaceuticals firm in Hyderabad, nearly 1,900 workers produce more than 100 generic medicines, ranging from cholesterol and allergy treatments to antidepressants. The plant manufactures close to one billion oral doses every month with roughly three-quarters of output destined for the US market, it added. The scale of India's generic drug industry has made the country indispensable to global medicine supplies. Generic medicines account for about 90 per cent of prescriptions dispensed in the United States, while Indian manufacturers supply around 40 per cent of those medicines. Trump has proposed steep tariffs on imported generic drugs, including a 100 per cent levy from 2028 and a 200 per cent tariff a year later as part of a broader push to expand domestic manufacturing. However, industry executives and healthcare experts said that cost advantages built over decades make large-scale reshoring difficult, according to the report. According to industry estimates, producing most generic medicines in the United States could cost four times more than manufacturing them in India. Lower labour costs, faster factory construction timelines and extensive technical expertise continue to give Indian drugmakers a competitive edge. The industry's rise dates back to the 1970s, when India prioritised affordable access to medicines and developed strong capabilities in reverse-engineering and manufacturing pharmaceutical products at scale. While concerns over manufacturing quality once clouded the industry's reputation, leading drugmakers say regulatory oversight has strengthened significantly. Major producers now face frequent inspections by global regulators and have invested heavily in compliance systems. Industry leaders argue that rather than decoupling, the United States and India should deepen cooperation, particularly as both countries seek to reduce dependence on China for pharmaceutical ingredients and strengthen supply-chain resilience, according to The Star. --IANS

stories.headline: SC asks WhatsApp, others to list measures to prevent digital arrest, related cyber crimes
stories.title: SC asks WhatsApp, others to list measures to prevent digital arrest, related cyber crimes
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 10: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it about their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country. In an order uploaded on the website with regard to the hearing conducted on October 29 in a suo motu case titled ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked WhatsApp and like intermediaries to simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C (Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre). The bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, has listed the plea for further consideration on November 23. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for WhatsApp, had told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken. He had said the platform was working on a software to identify suspicious accounts and warn users. “WhatsApp LLC (A Meta company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes. They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C,” the bench said in its order. The top court, on October 29, had said financial institutions must be held accountable for digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds, emphasising that banks should be required to compensate victims for losses suffered where an investigation establishes that the fraud occurred due to the institution's failure to exercise due diligence. “We reiterate and emphasize that the regulatory measures proposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must mandate and incorporate suitable provisions that require financial institutions to indemnify victims of digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds and pay suitable compensation not less than the amount lost by the customer, where it is established that the fraud or crime occurred due to the failure on the part of the financial institution to exercise due diligence in preventing or reporting the act/incident,” the bench said in the order. During the hearing, the CJI had questioned why banks could not intervene when customers suddenly attempted to transfer unusually large sums of money that were inconsistent with their established transaction patterns. “We have also emphasised in the past various preventive safeguards that must be mandated for every financial institution. These may include temporarily suspending unusual or suspicious transactions inconsistent with the account's past transaction history, automatically intimating such transactions to the nearest police station, and subsequently physically verifying the reported transactions to ascertain their genuineness,” the order said. In order to ensure effective implementation of the regulatory measures proposed by the RBI, as well as the directions issued, the bench further directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions before this court on the next date of hearing. Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, the bench had said the proposed RBI regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability. The CJI had said the bench would first examine the proposed RBI Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, before permitting the regulatory process to proceed. The directions are proposed to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31. Describing banks as a "protective umbrella" for vulnerable customers, the CJI had said financial institutions possess information about their account holders, including their transaction histories, and should use that knowledge to prevent fraud before money leaves an account. Attorney General R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, told the bench that substantial work had been undertaken to improve the detection of suspicious transactions and strengthen preventive mechanisms within the banking system. opening: New Delhi, Nov 10: The Supreme Court has asked WhatsApp and other intermediaries to apprise it about their proposed measures to prevent digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes in the country.

In an order uploaded on the website with regard to the hearing conducted on October 29 in a suo motu case titled ‘In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents’, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked WhatsApp and like intermediaries to simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C (Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre).

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for WhatsApp, had told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken.
He had said the platform was working on a software to identify suspicious accounts and warn users.

“WhatsApp LLC (A Meta company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes.
They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C,” the bench said in its order.

The top court, on October 29, had said financial institutions must be held accountable for digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds, emphasising that banks should be required to compensate victims for losses suffered where an investigation establishes that the fraud occurred due to the institution's failure to exercise due diligence.

“We reiterate and emphasize that the regulatory measures proposed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) must mandate and incorporate suitable provisions that require financial institutions to indemnify victims of digital arrest scams and other cyber frauds and pay suitable compensation not less than the amount lost by the customer, where it is established that the fraud or crime occurred due to the failure on the part of the financial institution to exercise due diligence in preventing or reporting the act/incident,” the bench said in the order.

During the hearing, the CJI had questioned why banks could not intervene when customers suddenly attempted to transfer unusually large sums of money that were inconsistent with their established transaction patterns.
“We have also emphasised in the past various preventive safeguards that must be mandated for every financial institution.

These may include temporarily suspending unusual or suspicious transactions inconsistent with the account's past transaction history, automatically intimating such transactions to the nearest police station, and subsequently physically verifying the reported transactions to ascertain their genuineness,” the order said.

In order to ensure effective implementation of the regulatory measures proposed by the RBI, as well as the directions issued, the bench further directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions before this court on the next date of hearing.

Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, the bench had said the proposed RBI regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability.

stories.title: Indian sports wrap, November 10: Boxer Ambekar Meetei reaches 50kg semifinals, assures India of medal at Youth Olympics
stories.summary: Here are India’s major updates, scores, and results from the world of sports on Tuesday, November 10.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Boxer Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei on Tuesday assured India of a medal in the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal after defeating Namibia’s Abraham Kalenga to advance to the semifinals of the men’s 50kg category.
Meetei won via Referee Stops Contest (RSC) in the first round of his quarterfinal bout which ended after 1 minute 57 seconds.
He will face Izzon Jeffrey Arevalo of Colombia in the semifinal on Wednesday.
India has already won three silver and five bronze medals in the Youth Olympics.

The International Schools Sports Organisation (ISSO) team delivered an encouraging performance at the ISF World School Golf Championship 2026 in Morocco, with young golfer Devvrat winning a bronze medal in the Under-15 category.
“Devvrat’s bronze medal is a proud moment for ISSO and Indian school sport.

At ISSO, we are committed to providing young athletes with international exposure and opportunities to compete against the best,” Aakanksha Thapak, Director, International Schools Sports Organisation (ISSO), said.
The Indian contingent, comprising six student-athletes, also secured fifth place in the overall team event, competing against 18 other teams from across the world.
“These experiences help them build confidence, develop their skills and prepare for bigger challenges ahead.
Congratulations to the entire Indian contingent on their performance,” Thapak added.

Held from November 2 to 8 in Taghazout-Agadir, Morocco, the championship brought together 19 teams, providing a global platform for young golfers to showcase their talent and compete at the highest level of school sport.

The overall fifth-place finish in the team event further underlined the competitive spirit and potential of the Indian contingent, as the six student-golfers gained valuable exposure by competing against international school teams.

stories.headline: Major Gen Mukesh Sharma takes charge as ADG NCC for J&K, Ladakh
stories.title: Major Gen Mukesh Sharma takes charge as ADG NCC for J&K, Ladakh
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 10: Major General Mukesh Sharma, who on Tuesday took over as the Additional Director General of the National Cadet Corps (NCC) Directorate for the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, outlined a vision to expand the organisation's outreach, empower youth and modernise its training programmes. Under the theme "Envision and Evolve: Empowering Youth, Strengthening NCC, Building the Nation", Sharma said he would focus on expanding NCC's presence in schools and colleges, particularly in remote, rural and border areas; empowering young cadets, especially girls; and making training more contemporary and relevant. Emphasising the NCC's guiding principles of "Unity and Discipline", he said the organisation aimed to develop confident, disciplined and responsible young citizens equipped with leadership qualities and a spirit of service. Highlighting the achievements of 20 girl cadets who successfully crossed the 5,578-metre-high Parang La Pass during the Aparajita Expedition, Sharma described it as a shining example of their courage, determination and leadership. "Efforts would be made to create more such opportunities for girl cadets and ensure that geographical challenges did not restrict young people from joining the NCC," he told reporters after taking over as the new chief of NCC in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh region. Stressing the need to modernise the organisation, he said training would be made more engaging and relevant to changing times, while teamwork and partnerships with educational institutions, civil administration and other stakeholders would be strengthened. Sharma urged the young cadets to dream big, embrace challenges, become physically fit, keep off drugs and continuously develop their skills. "NCC is not merely about uniforms, drills and parades; it is about building character, leadership and responsible citizens," he said. He also appreciated the contribution of NCC officers and staff at the grassroots level in shaping young cadets into disciplined and responsible citizens, and sought continued support from the Jammu and Kashmir government, Ladakh administration, educational institutions, parents and media. Describing media as an important partner in highlighting the achievements and contributions of cadets, he said the aim was to reach more youths, create greater opportunities and build a stronger NCC for a stronger nation.
